projects.title: Pranayama
projects.description: It all began with a breath. With Pranayama, we created a digital space where life's natural rhythm could be felt in every corner of the design. Our challenge was to convey calm, presence and clarity, while guiding visitors towards transformative conscious breathing sessions. From structure to every color, we built a clean site, connected with nature and Kenneth's intention, its creator. The collaboration was as fluid as breath itself, and reminded us that when client and creator flow in harmony, projects breathe on their own.

projects.title: HiPower
projects.description: After calm came expansion. With HiPower, the challenge wasn't just visual, but deeply technical: positioning the brand as a leader in solar energy for industries and businesses. From the start, we knew this site had to be as fast and powerful as the energy source it represents. Between lines of code and SEO strategies, we designed an experience that transmits strength and reliability, without sacrificing beauty. Aerial videos showed the magnitude of their projects, and making everything load in seconds was our trial by fire. This project made us grow as a team: it demanded precision, technical knowledge and a new understanding of what it means to give power... from the web.

projects.title: Terciopelo
projects.description: After connecting with energy, came the moment to transform. With Terciopelo Beauty, Nicky gave us just two words: tarot and esotericism. And with that, we opened the doors to a creative universe where beauty isn't just aesthetic, it's ritual. We designed a site that reflects their rebellious, sensitive and expressive spirit: a salon where every appointment is an act of personal magic. The booking system was key, but what really made this project vibrate was its visual identity, unique and daring, created with artificial intelligence tools to bring every icon and image to life. Terciopelo was our space to play, explore and let the mystical guide the design. Our most creative side found its favorite card here.

projects.title: Bohemian
projects.description: After connecting with energy, came the moment to transform. With The Bohemian, we created an experience that celebrates authenticity and natural beauty. A digital space that breathes creative freedom and connects with those seeking to express their true essence. This project allowed us to explore new frontiers of design, creating a visual identity that fuses organic elements with modern technology, resulting in a platform that invites users to reconnect with their most authentic side.

faq.subtitle: FAQ
faq.titlePart2: about web design in Costa Rica

faqs.question: How do I know if I really need a new website or if adjusting the current one is enough?
faqs.answer: If your current site fails to make people understand what you offer within seconds, doesn't generate measurable inquiries, or works poorly on mobile, it's usually not a "minor adjustment." If the issue is just outdated content or a specific section, adjustments may suffice.

faqs.question: What information do I need to have ready before hiring web design?
faqs.answer: A clear definition of what you sell, who you sell to, main services/products, service area, main site goal (inquiries, sales, scheduling, catalog), and basic brand materials (logo/colors if they exist). If you have visual references, they help align style without improvising.

faqs.question: What should a "high-quality website" deliver beyond looking nice?
faqs.answer: Message clarity, simple navigation, good mobile experience, reasonable load times, working forms, and a structure that guides the user to a concrete action.

faqs.question: What can I realistically expect after publishing my website?
faqs.answer: More trust and credibility, better ability to convert interested visitors into inquiries, and a solid foundation for campaigns or organic growth. It's not realistic to expect automatic sales without a traffic source or a clear offer.

faqs.question: What should be clear in a quote to avoid surprises?
faqs.answer: Scope of sections/pages, what's included and what's not, revision rounds, timelines per stage, whether it includes e-commerce, whether it includes publishing, and how out-of-scope changes will be handled.

faqs.question: Why are some websites very cheap and others more expensive?
faqs.answer: Usually the difference lies in the level of work on structure, prototyping, custom design, revisions, development quality, mobile testing, and post-launch support. Many cheap websites cut corners on those layers and the cost appears later in rebuilding or "patching."

faqs.question: What if I don't have professional photos or ready text?
faqs.answer: You can move forward with provisional material, but perceived quality may drop. Ideally, define what content is essential for launch and what can be improved later without blocking the release.

faqs.question: When does a landing page make sense vs. a full website?
faqs.answer: Landing: when you have a clear offer and want a single action (request/quote). Full site: when the user needs more information to decide (services, trust, proof, questions).

faqs.question: What's the practical difference between "web design" and "web development"?
faqs.answer: Design defines structure, experience, and how the value proposition is communicated. Web development implements functionality, performance, and integrations. They are distinct but complementary stages.

faqs.question: What exactly does "web development" include and what's left out?
faqs.answer: It includes production implementation, base performance, essential security (SSL), agreed integrations, QA, and publishing. Left out is anything not specified: functionalities with private logic, new unplanned integrations, massive content, and scope changes without estimation.

faqs.question: How do you prevent the project from becoming "patches" or becoming unstable over time?
faqs.answer: With clear scope, maintainable technical structure, QA before publishing, and change control. The priority is for the site to remain understandable, stable, and easy to evolve without breaking with each adjustment.

faqs.question: What if during the project I realize I need more features?
faqs.answer: The change is documented, estimated, and prioritized. We prefer to formalize adjustments instead of "adding things" without control, to protect stability, timelines, and quality.

faqs.question: Can I hire development if I already have a design/prototype, or if my site already exists?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can implement from an existing design or work on an already published site, as long as the scope is clear. If the current base limits performance or maintenance, partial or full re-implementation is recommended. Important note: we can work on an existing design but NOT on an already-built website. Most are on site builders like Wix or WordPress. We don't work with or maintain those systems. Even if it's built in code, we can't guarantee the quality of the code we deliver since it wasn't structured by us, and often doing it right means starting from scratch.

faqs.question: How do you handle integrations and automations to reduce manual work?
faqs.answer: We define them based on your real workflow (lead capture, scheduling, orders, communication). We implement agreed integrations (forms, scheduling, payments, CRM/email) and leave the process organized so it doesn't depend on chats for everything.

faqs.question: How "custom" can the development be without becoming a giant system?
faqs.answer: It depends on rules, roles, and flows. If they're specific adjustments, they're integrated within the site. If there's private logic or internal processes (dashboards, portals, ticketing with rules), it's approached as a custom module with its own specification and estimation.

faqs.question: How do you guarantee quality before publishing?
faqs.answer: With an exit checklist: mobile testing, forms, flows, integrations, and final performance and stability review. Ideally we use a staging environment before production to validate without affecting the live site.

faqs.question: What access and ownership do I get at the end of the project?
faqs.answer: You get the access and operational control of the site (accounts, domains/hosting if applicable, and the admin environment). We also leave minimal documentation for continuity and handoff.

faqs.question: What happens after launch if I need changes, support, or evolution?
faqs.answer: You can work on specific improvements by scope, or continue with maintenance/evolution to ensure continuity, updates, and improvements without improvisation. The goal is for the project not to be "abandoned" over time.
